pr_comments:
Does this message also need to be updated?
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/c7a2c0648a0fad7dc1f98c18702d1a4c1d72bcc2/src/Identity/Extensions.Core/src/Resources.resx#L193

I think this test needs to be updated too.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/c95ee2b051814b787b07f55ff224d03d550aafeb/src/Identity/test/Identity.Test/PasswordValidatorTest.cs#L149
@Kahbazi Thanks again for review. I've updated the error message in the test, and also added a test case with the new behavior.
Any idea if there is any specific file that should be updated in this PR to track the breaking change?

I also find this type that need to be updated.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/c95ee2b051814b787b07f55ff224d03d550aafeb/src/Identity/src/Core/PasswordOptions.cs#L28

I think its probably best to take a compromise approach, seems fine to change the default implementation and comments to use Unicode Upper/Lower, but I think there's no harm in leaving these virtual, and let people continue to override the behavior to implement Upper/Lower as they see fit.
@HaoK, I've added virtual back. Do you want me to use `Rune` instead of char.IsUpper and char.IsLower?
Yeah if @GrabYourPitchforks suggests using Rune, I think we should listen to his guidance on correctness there :)

The suggestion was that the methods `IsLower(char)` and `IsUpper(char)` weren't correct in the first place and that we should no longer use these methods. The issue https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/23562 still needs to be fleshed out, including exactly what problem it's trying to solve. The issue as reported concerns itself only with German characters, but is it really indicating a larger issue that also affects our Chinese and Japanese and Korean users? That really deserves a more thorough discussion. I think this PR, while well-intentioned, is premature until a plan of action has been settled on there.
Thank you for this, but it's too big a beaking risk for now.

comments: Hi - can you let us know what type of project you are using when this happens?

Oh nooooo

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/src/Identity/Extensions.Core/src/PasswordValidator.cs#L108

@HaoK can we change this to use [IsUpper](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.char.isupper?view=netcore-3.1) or IsLower?

(Unless someone would like to give us a PR, it's a nice first issue)
I've opened a PR for this. But please note that this might be a breaking change.

It's definitely a breaking change. The APIs are even publicly documented as concerning themselves only with ASCII, not with arbitrary Unicode characters. If the team decides to accept a change here it should be documented.

A nit: prefer to use `Rune.IsUpper` instead of `char.ToUpper`, as it's more correct. Not that it's all that common to use supplementary characters in passwords anyway, but if we're going to check this, may as well do it right. :)

Also, the team should reconsider whether these methods should be virtual at all. A method documented as "returns true if the input character is uppercase ASCII" has only one correct implementation. There's no need for an override.

@GrabYourPitchforks I've removed "virtual" from my PR. That's a breaking change too, but hopefully no one will be overriding these methods in a real code.

Regarding the Rune, I'm not very familiar with them, a quick look at docs shows there's an explicit conversion from char to Rune, should I cast the char to Rune and pass the result to Rune.IsUpper and Rune.IsLower? or there's another approach?

Also consider that if you're trying to make a system that supports multiple languages throughout the world, some languages don't even have a concept of uppercase or lowercase characters. Any discussion regarding making the password validator more amenable to non-ASCII characters has to include these considerations.

@GrabYourPitchforks Great. I'll wait for the team here to decide whether they accept the breaking change(s) introduced or not. Given that a very quick search on GitHub shows [a usage](https://github.com/delta-it/Coco.Web/blob/786cbba181ea7b249fb5dbe58b64ec282d2b23e8/Source/Coco.Server/Coco.Api.Framework/Security/CustomPasswordValidator.cs) where the PasswordValidator is inherited and the virtual methods are overriden with the same base implementation.

Oof, ok this is horribly broken and may be widely breaking if we attempt to change it (as is all our localization in general here).

@Youssef1313 you can replace the validator yourself, via your own implementation and DI, and that's why you're going to have to solve it for yourself.
